quorum.kill_rule: six claims and the standing instruction. THE SELECTION FAILED OPEN on the gates' own fixtures and their shared resolver — two lanes quoted the same sentence about what gate C and gate D read and both were right — and no case in the suite could have caught it. The first fix over-corrected and was measured collapsing the saving from seven PRs to two.
refuted_claims: That gate C reads only the built binary and docs/audits/surface_audit.csv, and gate D only the binary, README.md and that CSV. Both run scripts/dogfood/lib/binary.sh; gate C evaluates tests/fixtures/dogfood/local-files.yaml two ways; gate D runs everything against the whole fixture tree and opens Cargo.toml.

That tests/* and scripts/* outside scripts/dogfood/ are harmless for the two gates. Both fixtures and the shared resolver live under exactly those prefixes, so a PR editing the very fixture gate C compares would have skipped gate C.
That closing the hole is free. Selecting the whole of scripts/dogfood/ was measured against the same 25 PRs and collapsed the saving from seven to two.
That an absent base is handled. The action fell back to HEAD~1, so a workflow_dispatch re-run of a twenty-commit branch was classified from ONE commit.
That the workflow cases assert on what the workflow does. A bare substring test is satisfied by a comment carrying the same words.
That the dogfood steps sum to the job's 25.2 minutes. 9.0 + 6.2 + 6.1 + 3.8 is 25.1; the 0.1 is setup and checkout.
That the roadmap row carries the measured figure. It still ended 'Measured version: 56% of PRs', a number corrected everywhere else.

That 'all the new cases are RED against origin/main' says as much as it sounds like. Four of them read the workflow files, so the claim holds only because the proof reverts all three non-Rust files together.

systems: Bazel (target-level change pruning from the action graph, not from path globs)
Nix (a derivation is rebuilt exactly when its input closure hash moves)
Kubernetes Prow (run_if_changed regexes per presubmit job)
Buck2 (dep-file-based incrementality: the inputs a rule actually read)
crux.verdict: accept(every surveyed system prunes work by an input closure rather than by a directory name, and the two that prune by regex -- Prow -- are the ones that ship the failure this round found: a job whose real inputs drift out of its pattern silently stops running. forjar cannot compute a true input closure for a shell gate, so it does the next honest thing: the closure is DERIVED BY READING THE TWO GATES and a test re-derives it on every run, which is Buck2's dep-file idea done by hand. Where forjar is WORSE than all four: the selection is a hand-written allow-list in one shell case statement, and its correctness rests on that one re-derivation case rather than on the build system observing what the gate opened. Where it is better than Prow: a not-selected gate prints NOT-SELECTED rather than nothing, so a reader can tell a skipped measurement from a passing one.)
